rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Skara Brae 1.1 Gameplay 1.2 Resources & Waste Management 1.3 Round End & Scoring 1.4 Action Tile Overview 1.5 Village & Special Cards Skara Brae In this tactical resource management game for 1-4 players, you lead a Stone Age community on the Orkney Islands. The goal is to gather resources to support your settlers and manage waste (Midden) to accumulate the most Victory Points (VP). Gameplay The game lasts exactly 4 rounds. Each round consists of 3 turns per player. A turn consists of the following steps: Select Card: Choose 1 available Village Card from the display and resolve it immediately. Assign Workers: Place your Large Worker (and up to 3 Small Workers) on your Action Tiles. Actions are resolved from top to bottom. Retrieve Workers: Collect all workers back for your next turn. Resources & Waste Management Resources are stored in your storage area. Each slot holds exactly 1 resource. The Slider: If you gain more resources than slots available, the slider moves to the right. This increases waste production and results in negative VP at the end. Midden (Waste): Occupies storage slots and can only be removed via the "Clean" action. Round End & Scoring After 3 turns, the round ends: Feeding: Each settler without a roof must be fed 1 Food, or they are discarded. Waste Production: Gain Midden according to the slider's position (minus Utensil bonuses). End of Game: After 4 rounds, points are awarded for played cards (Settlers, Roofs, Stone Balls), track progress, and upgraded Action Tiles. Midden and slider position result in negative points. Action Tile Overview Each tile can be activated once by a Small Worker and once by the Large Worker per turn. Action Icon Effect Gather 🧺 Gain basic resources (Shells, Barley, Seaweed, Wool, Stone, or Wood). Cook 🍲 Process raw materials into Food or crafting materials (Hides, Bone, Wool). Furnish 🏺 Spend Wool or Hides to advance on the Furnishing Track (VP multiplier). Trade 🤝 Exchange resources for Trade Track progress or Goods Tokens. Clean 🧹 Remove Midden tokens from storage and move the slider to the left. Craft 🔨 Flip an Action Tile to its upgraded side (better effects & 2 VP). Village & Special Cards Type Effect Settlers Placed in rows; trigger immediate harvests and provide ongoing bonuses. Roofs Protect settlers from hunger at the end of the round (saving 1 Food). Utensils Increase the hearth limit for Cooking or reduce waste production. Stone Balls Grant immediate Skaill Knives (wild resource for harvests or VP).

[Rating: 2/10] Players take their actions and do their combos without even a blink in someone else’s direction. This is not one competitive game; it is solo gamers sitting at the same table. I used to really enjoy Garphill games - now… I don’t get excited. Both game gameplay here and the art are technically pretty, but lifeless.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA. While the core concept is clever and engaging, the game's flaws become apparent after 4 or 5 plays. As a multiplayer experience, it relies heavily on drafting the right cards at the right time. This represents the only form of player interaction, yet it feels entirely dictated by the luck of the draw. The second half of the game shifts into a spatial puzzle reminiscent of Ezra and Nehemiah. [Rating: 3/10] I hesitate to rate this a three as I don’t agree it’s bad, per se. It’s just boring. The decision space didn’t do anything for me.  Why it’s a three instead of four is down to the “play again” aspect. I never want to play this again.

I think that's reflective of where Shem has gone as a designer: over-the-top complication without adding any depth or thinkiness. I think Shipwrights Redux is the much better game. [Rating: 5/10] Pretty good resource management euro. Balancing 16 different resources is frustrating in fun way and rarely have I been playing a euro and thought "oh no, I am getting way too many resources", as having too many resources also generates midden that has to be cleaned up. Not a game I will actively seek to play, and if so I don't see a point of playing it any other way than solo, but as a solitaire puzzle it does it's job.

[Rating: 5/10] Multiplayer solitaire. The card selection is some minor interaction at least but the game is mostly individual busy work.

[Rating: 5/10] Overly convoluted resource manipulation game with near zero player interaction.   The card selection is the only interactive part of the game. After everyone has selected the card they wanted out of few options, they sit there in silence running their resource engine. This part is simultaneous, so you never know if people are playing the game correctly. After some time you ask if everyone is ready, and then you select a new card, and again sit in silence converting resources to other resources.
